messages:
support_james: FYI customer Storely is seeing recurring 504s and very high tail latency on hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC. Lots of reports in the last 30m. Request ids: r:storely:ac:32f9.. Many are p95+ timeouts.

oncall-erica: copying. any repro steps from the customer?

support_james: customer provided a short repro: repeated small chat requests (~40-60 tokens) at 150 qps for one tenant. They say it degrades after ~5–10 minutes and then a long tail of 5–12s per request, lots of 504s. They sent logs showing queue depth saturating.

infra_sre: looking at metrics now — hosted-gateway queue depth spiked to 320 for that shard (max configured 320). continuous-batcher backlog length jumped at the same time. p99 dequeue latency hit 6.3s.

samir_prodeng: that matches a KV-cache spinup pattern. If many new prefixes come in, continuous batching can stall while kvcache is populated and the batcher waits for model warmup. We saw similar earlier but usually capped by our queue depth.

devex_elaine: customer sample repro curl? asked for it but they sent a short script. We'll attach a minimal repro: 
```bash
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b","input":"hello","max_tokens":40}' &\ndone\nwait\n```

customer_ops: they ran that in a single zone against hosted and reported errors start after ~200s.

deploy-bot: deploy event: config change to gateway autoscaler at 2026-02-18T08:50:03Z (no restarts).

oncall-erica: initial mitigation suggestions?

infra_sre: immediate actions we can do: 1) increase gateway request_queue.max_depth for that shard from 320 -> 512 (risk: memory). 2) apply tenant-specific rate-limits temporarily. 3) force fallback to a lower-memory model variant for that tenant. 4) flip continuous_batching: false for the tenant to use passthrough batching.

support_james: customer asked for a quick fix without code changes — they prefer a config change.

samir_prodeng: I'd do (4) + (1) as short-term: disabling continuous batching eliminates the prefix-wait behavior and lets us serve individual requests faster, and increasing depth buys breathing room. Also check autoscaler threshold: it didn't trigger because the scale policy waits on average throughput, not queue spike.

infra_sre: ran a dry change in staging: toggling continuous_batching for a tenant dropped p99 from ~6s -> ~160ms under similar load. We can roll to prod for Storely if approved.

oncall-erica: proceed with toggle and depth bump. I'll coordinate a short maintenance window.

devex_elaine: logging note — add a temporary per-request tag to correlate: X-Request-Triage:storely-repro.

support_james: customer agreed to apply changes. They want repro steps so they can validate.

samir_prodeng: reproduction checklist for them: 1) run the curl loop above against their tenant; 2) monitor header X-Redwood-Request-ID in responses; 3) after 3m if errors start, notify us with a sample request-id and time window. Also ask them to include whether requests have identical or slightly different prompts — high prefix variance worsens kvcache warmups.

infra_sre: change applied at 09:45 UTC: continuous_batching=false for tenant storely-tenant-id-998, gateway.request_queue.max_depth bumped to 512 on shard-7.

deploy-bot: changelog: tenant-config-update storely-tenant-id-998 at 2026-02-18T09:45:22Z.

oncall-erica: monitoring now: queue depth falling, dequeue p99 trending down.

customer_ops: customer reports immediate drop in 504s and tail latency reduced to under 200ms. They saw one brief spike when we toggled but then stabilized.

support_james: closing loop with customer. They asked if this is permanent.

samir_prodeng: next steps: 1) root cause analysis: why autoscaler didn't react. 2) add a heuristic to detect KV coldspin (high prefix churn) and auto-disable continuous batching for affected tenants. 3) consider increasing default queue max depth or make it adaptive per-tenant. 4) surface this pattern in our runbook for SRE/Support.

devex_elaine: I'll draft a customer-facing postmortem blurb and update the internal runbook with repro steps and mitigation commands.

oncall-erica: thanks team. tagging: @infra_sre please file a follow-up incident ticket with traces and the exact metric windows.

infra_sre: filing incident: INC-2026-0218-1771 with attached traces and batcher logs.

support_james: marking resolved for customer; will reopen if they see recurrences. :white_check_mark:
